ui_map.notes: Only visible layer items may exist in the UIA tree.
The canvas is a single self-drawn surface. UIA provides bounds only; drawing requires L4 input.

rules: Resolve the canvas coordinate transform immediately before every drag.
Do not reuse a point across a zoom, scroll, resize, DPI, or monitor change.
If calibration fails, disable L4 canvas input and escalate to NeedsHuman.
The drag start and end points must use the same coordinate-space contract.

workflows.name: T3.1 new canvas rectangle
pitfalls: A new document can discard unsaved work.
The active tool, color, and layer must be read back before drawing.
A visual assertion must tolerate anti-aliasing and compression artifacts.

workflows.name: T3.2 open PNG and mark region
pitfalls: The Save As dialog is cross-process.
The opened image size and zoom must be read back before resolving points.
Existing output files must not be overwritten silently.

workflows.name: T3.3 draw then rollback
pitfalls: Ctrl+Z behavior can merge multiple canvas actions.
A pixel snapshot is evidence and an anchor, not a guarantee that Paint can import it.
A failed rollback is an incident and must not be reported as success.

known_pitfalls: Canvas coordinates are not screen coordinates; zoom and scroll offsets must be applied for every write.
The canvas is self-drawn and has no actionable child-control tree.
The active drawing tool, color, and layer are implicit state and must be read back.
Anti-aliasing and alpha blending make exact pixel equality unreliable.
A drag interrupted mid-way can leave a partial stroke.
Layer selection determines where drawing lands; virtualized layer lists may instantiate only visible rows.
AI features may require network access and have unbounded latency; they are disabled.
The Save As dialog belongs to a Shell child process.
The PowerShell/UIA probe channel was not usable during this card, so all selector IDs are provisional until TASK-044 verifies them.

caveats: Canvas undo may merge several pointer events into one action or split one drag into several actions.
Ctrl+Z is documented by the adapter but must be verified with pixel evidence.
A pixel snapshot does not by itself guarantee a safe restore path.
